![Historical throughput: eight bars compare Tesseract and Python Indra under shared and partitioned application quotas; no native Rust measurement](../figures/signed-baseline-throughput.png)

![Historical successful-response p95: eight bars, with larger values indicating slower tail latency and no confidence intervals](../figures/signed-baseline-p95.png)

The historical study has 15 mostly English synthetic fixtures, each executed
three times. All eight cells have 45 successful responses. It cannot meet the
new multilingual quality requirement. At one CPU, concurrency was one; at two
CPUs, it was two. That changes both available CPU and offered load. The old load
generator was outside the application cgroup. These results must not be pooled
with the new experiment, which includes its load generator inside the common
CPU and memory limits.

Python Indra's historical shared-quota throughput exceeds its partitioned-quota
throughput. The partitions constrain Tika independently even while OCR quota is
idle; the measurements support investigating that deployment tradeoff. They do
not identify the cause independently of the complete stack. Tail latency worsens
under the partitioned configuration despite a better median. Therefore a single
throughput ratio is insufficient to select a production configuration.

Strict CER was 409/9029 for Tesseract and 131/9029 for Python Indra. The
whitespace-collapsed secondary view was 195/8924 versus 11/8924. These are repeated
measurements of the same 15 references, not 120 independent accuracy samples.
Whitespace materially changes the apparent advantage; strict and collapsed
metrics should remain adjacent in the new analysis.

## Frozen multilingual study

The [main manifest](../corpus-frozen.json) contains 33 primary pages in 19 document
clusters and eight separately reported challenges. The primary appearance mix is
19 printed, 11 handwritten and three mixed pages. English occurs on two primary
pages in one cluster; 51 of 87,515 NFC reference letters are English. All three
proportions are below 10%. This is a small, heterogeneous engineering corpus, not
a representative sample of every language, profession or production deployment.

The [always-math amendment](../audits/always-math-20261019/amendment.json) removes only the two text-only Indra arms after disclosed quick diagnostics, at the user's request. The six retained arms span 24 cells and 60 within-budget/cohort pairs. This is a prospective execution amendment, not a blind preregistration. Original protocols remain recoverable from the pinned source; inputs, references, scoring, seeds, repetition order and resource limits are unchanged. The [Indra 1.1 amendment](../audits/indra-1-1-20261020/amendment.json) binds both Indra arms to model revision `bd02167f` (tag v1.1.0, package indra-ocr 1.1.2) with math, LM beam search and dual-read routing enabled; it changes no protocol byte, and an artifact measured with another model lock is not reported under it.

This is a comparison of deployed configurations. Both Indra arms keep math
and FP32 enabled, but their native builds, packaging and session policies differ.
Rust stops spinning in inactive private pools between calls when using multiple
threads; the Python reference does not request that setting. Its effective
allow-spinning build default was not independently established, so nominal
protocol flags are not evidence that both processes use the same policy.
Python enables memory patterns; Rust disables them. Tesseract uses one OpenMP
thread at both budgets, while Indra's thread count follows the budget; offered
concurrency remains one. These differences prevent attributing a main-study
ratio to Rust versus Python alone, or claiming that each engine is individually
optimal. The separate matched-spinning diagnostic in
[native profiling](../../docs/native-profiling.md#idle-session-cpu-policy) uses
three already known inputs and retains its own producer and limitations; it
must not be pooled with this corpus or treated as a single-setting causal test.

The [protocol](../protocol.json) fixes Tika rendering, source/model hashes,
configuration identities, warmup, repetition order, CPU/memory policy and metrics
before OCR execution. The Rust evaluator records immutable input/reference and
output identities, HTTP failures and complete-body timing. Execution repetitions
are technical repeats; quality uses the declared first repetition. Paired
resampling draws complete document clusters, preserving within-document
dependence. Language, script, domain, appearance, reference quality and task type
are descriptive strata; small strata do not justify broad inferential claims.

Strict NFC code-point CER retains whitespace and punctuation. A separate
whitespace-collapsed CER qualifies transcription/layout effects. WER uses the
declared whitespace tokenizer and is omitted where that tokenization is
inappropriate. Public training overlap is unknown. Historical editorial
transcriptions and extracted PDF text have explicit reference qualifications.
Oracle crops are challenge inputs, never relabeled as full-page end-to-end OCR.

## Execution admission and all planned statuses

Without an admitted artifact every cell below is **unsubmitted**. Missing
measurements have no numeric value. To admit downloaded combined evidence, set
`OCR_EVALUATION_ROOT` and the independently selected full commit
`OCR_EVALUATION_SOURCE_SHA` together before rendering. An invalid artifact aborts
this notebook; it never falls back to the historical data or an empty study.

24 unique cells and 60 comparison identities, reviewer-selected source,

Cosign verification and the retained live OCI/cgroup acceptance receipts are

Each admitted budget shard also names the hardware it ran on, read from its own

The paired figure shows the prespecified fast PSM3 strict-CER view; `paired.csv`
also carries every other left arm and the collapsed-CER and WER differences with
their frozen intervals. The strata figure is descriptive: per arm and stratum
level for appearance, script and domain in the main primary cohort, a filled
strict-CER mark joined to an open whitespace-collapsed mark, faceted by CPU budget,
with the level's selected-case count in its label and each arm's scored/selected,
failures and metric limits in the artist receipt. Arms sit at fixed offsets that the
renderer keeps at least one mark diameter apart, so equal values stay visible per arm.
Small levels carry no interval and support no ranking. The workload figure's whiskers
span the three per-repetition values; they are a post-hoc descriptive addendum, not
an interval.

The compact table below uses the predeclared fast PSM3, Python math and Rust math
arms for readability. The exports retain all six arms, all six stratum axes and
all three metrics, including tokenizer eligibility and unavailable WER. Values
remain conditional on scoreable first attempts; coverage and failures travel with
each cell. Appearance/language strata describe this finite selection.

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    strata = pd.read_csv(report_directory / "study-data/summaries.csv")
    focus = ("tesseract-fast-psm3", "python-math-b64", "rust-math-b64")
    selected = strata[(strata.study == "main") & (strata.cohort == "primary") & strata.axis.isin(("appearance", "language")) &
                      strata.metric.isin(("cer", "cer_whitespace_collapsed")) & strata.variant.isin(focus)]
    def compact(group):
        strict, collapsed = (group[group.metric == metric].iloc[0] for metric in ("cer", "cer_whitespace_collapsed"))
        rate = lambda row: "no numeric" if pd.isna(row.micro_rate) else f"{100 * row.micro_rate:.1f}%"
        return f"{rate(strict)} · {rate(collapsed)} · {int(strict.scored_cases)}/{int(strict.selected_cases)}; F{int(strict.service_failures)}; M{int(strict.metric_limits)}"
    if not selected.empty:
        table = selected.groupby(["axis", "level", "cpus", "variant"]).apply(compact, include_groups=False).unstack("variant").reindex(columns=focus)
        table.columns.name = "strict · collapsed CER · scored/selected; failures; metric limits"
        display_table(table)
```

Strict and collapsed CER stay adjacent in the strata figure and the table. Both
condition on scoreable first attempts; the row labels retain service failures and
metric limits. Paired
intervals come unchanged from the Rust scorer's frozen document-cluster draws.
Each pair can use a different joint-success subset; its eligible case/cluster and
reference-unit counts and both arms' exclusions remain visible. A conditional
paired difference is not a whole-arm benefit or a population superiority claim.
The laboratory supplement has no intervals; challenge summaries remain separate
and descriptive. CER may exceed 100%; plots neither cap it nor use logarithmic
axes that would hide zero.

Whole-main throughput covers all 41 primary-plus-challenge cases across all three
technical repetitions; it is not repeated as a primary/language throughput.
Higher throughput and lower latency are favorable. Successful complete-body
latencies use linear type7 empirical quantiles of all admitted successful
non-warmup attempts; they are finite observations, with failed-attempt counts
alongside them. Failed termination times
remain in the raw export. A missing successful sample yields no latency mark.
Neither repetitions nor high quantiles create independent documents or a
production tail guarantee. CPU budgets remain separate; a budget difference is
not by itself isolated CPU scaling.

Tesseract receives the prespecified per-case language hint and PSM; Indra uses its
native script handling without those request headers. Cases include qualified
editorial references and oracle crops; no single quality ranking applies to all
production domains. All arms are serial at concurrency 1; this does not test
cross-request continuous batching. Startup includes Docker create/start and
readiness polling after model-inventory hashing has warmed the file cache; it is
not storage-cold startup or request latency. Parent charged-memory lifetime peaks
include setup/sentinel/startup, while request CPU deltas include warmup. Model
cache pages populated outside the parent can remain charged elsewhere. Shared
3GiB/zero-swap accounting includes Tika, optional OCR and the load generator.

## Descriptive views by legal layout, length and recorded traits

These three views were added after the measurement as a reporting addendum. They
read the exported per-case rows, run no OCR or rescoring, and carry no interval or
ranking. The legal view sets the prespecified strict CER beside whitespace-collapsed
CER and WER on the modern legal pages. The length view applies the corpus plan's
prespecified reference-length bins. The trait view groups pages by the typography,
layout and condition traits the frozen manifest records; provenance flags are left
out.

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    import analysis
    data_directory = report_directory / "study-data"
    reproduced = analysis.reproduces_summaries(data_directory)
    legal_rows, legal_languages, legal_references = analysis.legal(data_directory)
    display(Markdown(f"The case-level aggregation below reproduces all {reproduced} exported domain summaries. "
                     + analysis.legal_text(legal_rows, legal_languages, legal_references)))
    display_table(pd.DataFrame(legal_rows))
    length_rows, length_note = analysis.length_bins(data_directory)
    display(Markdown(length_note))
    display_table(pd.DataFrame(length_rows))
    trait_rows = analysis.traits(data_directory, study.frozen_studies()["main"]["manifest"])
    display(Markdown(analysis.traits_text(trait_rows)))
    display_table(pd.DataFrame(trait_rows))
else:
    display(Markdown("No admitted artifact: there are no descriptive views."))
```

## Startup and parent resource snapshots

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    resources = pd.read_csv(report_directory / "study-data/resources.csv")
    cpu_view = resources[["study", "cpus", "variant"]].copy()
    cpu_view["start to ready (s)"] = resources.startup_ready_ms / 1000
    cpu_view["warmup + workload CPU (s)"] = resources.warmup_workload_cpu_usage_usec / 1_000_000
    cpu_view["admission to captured driver-end CPU (s)"] = resources.cpu_since_admission_usage_usec / 1_000_000
    display_table(cpu_view)
    memory_view = resources[["study", "cpus", "variant"]].copy()
    memory_view["observed parent lifetime peak (MiB)"] = resources.parent_memory_peak_observed_bytes / 1024**2
    memory_view["memory.events at driver-end snapshot"] = resources.memory_events_after_driver
    display_table(memory_view)
```

These are existing parent-cgroup counters, rather than sums of process RSS.
The journal CPU delta starts before warmup and ends after the workload and
bookkeeping; it excludes process/model startup. The separate admission-to-driver
snapshot delta also includes startup and driver cleanup, but ends **before** the
outer controller removes the sentinel and retires the parent. It is not an
HTTP-only or cohort-specific CPU measurement. Readiness includes container
create/start and polling after model inventory has warmed the host file cache.

The observed lifetime memory peak includes setup/sentinel/startup and is never
subtracted from a prior peak. Model file-cache pages populated outside the parent
can remain charged elsewhere. The CSV retains all four current/peak snapshots,
all memory-event keys and both explicit counter windows. Nonzero events remain
visible; this reporting addendum introduces no new outcome exclusion or threshold.
All resource rows remain separate by arm, study and actual CPU budget.

## Laboratory supplement

The [separate Portuguese supplement](../laboratory-supplement/README.md) contains
two chemistry methods crops from distinct public papers. The evaluated crops
contain no English reference letters; their surrounding source pages may contain
English. It is not a collection of complete laboratory reports or clinical
documents. With only two document clusters, the supplement reports descriptive
point estimates and failures, with **zero bootstrap resamples and no confidence
intervals**. The published acquisition amendment preserves original hashes, recovers two
exact HTML originals and retains two changed live responses as audit evidence.
The separately hashed operational acquisition index omits the two unavailable
metadata originals without replacing frozen inputs, references or protocols.

## Results

Every number in this section and the next is read at render time from the
exported study-data tables of the admitted evidence. Quality uses the declared
first repetition; performance uses all three. Strata, length bins, traits and the
per-repetition spread are descriptive and carry no interval.

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    import analysis
    data_directory = report_directory / "study-data"
    display(Markdown("### Quality\n\n" + analysis.quality(data_directory) + "\n\n" + analysis.paired(data_directory)))
    worse = analysis.strata_versus_tesseract(data_directory, worse=True)
    display(Markdown("### Strata where Indra is worse than the best Tesseract setting\n\n" + analysis.worse_strata_text(worse)))
    if worse:
        display_table(pd.DataFrame(worse))
    display(Markdown("### Laboratory crops\n\n" + analysis.laboratory(data_directory)))
    display(Markdown("### Math markup in the Indra outputs\n\n" + analysis.math_text(data_directory)))
    costs = analysis.cpu_cost(data_directory)
    display(Markdown("### Performance and CPU cost\n\n" + analysis.cpu_cost_text(costs, new_study["hosts"]) + "\n\n" + analysis.repetition_text(data_directory)))
    display_table(pd.DataFrame(costs))
    titles = {item["stem"]: item["title"] for item in study_figures["plots"]}
    display(Markdown("### Reading the figures\n\n" + "\n".join(f"- **{titles[stem]}.** {reading}" for stem, reading in analysis.readings(data_directory).items() if stem in titles)))
else:
    display(Markdown("No admitted artifact: there are no multilingual results."))
```

## Discussion

```{python}
if new_study["measurements"]:
    display(Markdown("\n\n".join(analysis.discussion(data_directory, new_study["hosts"]))))
```

These readings describe one execution of the small, heterogeneous frozen corpus
described above, with unknown training overlap and editorial reference
qualifications. The paired
intervals are the only inferential statements and are not adjusted for
multiplicity. The strata, legal, length, trait and per-repetition views were added
after the results were known; they describe these documents and runs and do not
rank engines for a script, language, domain or deployment. Tesseract receives a
per-case language hint and Indra does not, the two Indra arms differ in build and
session policy, and both budgets run at concurrency 1, so no ratio here isolates
an engine, a language binding or a CPU budget.
